req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The delete endpoint (POST /<id>/delete) must: (1) remove the post row from the DB and return 302 to '/' for the post's author (positive/EP); (2) return 403 when a non-author authenticated user attempts deletion (negative/DT); (3) return 404 when the post id does not exist (boundary/BVA — id just beyond the last known row); (4) return 302 and confirm row is gone after deletion (STC — state transition from 'post exists' to 'post absent'); (5) return 401/302-to-login when unauthenticated (NEG). Each test is self-contained with its own temp DB, uses exact status codes, and verifies DB state directly to kill constant-mutation and comparison-flip mutants.

tests.name: test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_and_removes_row
preconditions: Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
expected: Post id=2 no longer exists in the database
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_and_removes_row():
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        row = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (2,)).fetchone()
    assert row is None

test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_and_removes_row()

tests.name: test_delete_post_state_transition_post_absent_after_delete
preconditions: Post id=1 exists and is authored by James (author_id=5)
actions: Verify post id=1 exists before deletion
Verify post id=1 no longer exists after deletion
expected: Pre-delete: post id=1 row is present
Delete response status code is exactly 302
Delete response Location header is exactly '/'
Post-delete: post id=1 row is absent
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_post_state_transition_post_absent_after_delete():
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    with app.app_context():
        pre = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (1,)).fetchone()
    assert pre is not None
    assert pre['id'] == 1
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        post = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = ?', (1,)).fetchone()
    assert post is None

test_delete_post_state_transition_post_absent_after_delete()
